note: DRAFT cases for the Shared Team Directory (academy/team/directory.js). Not wired into run.js; validated by tests/test_academy_team.js. Community is the Drama Creek demo; people are fictional.

cases.title: Claire hands a governance question to Amanda
cases.scenario: A homeowner asks Claire whether the board can change the fence rules without a homeowner vote. The documents have a rules-and-regulations clause and an amendment clause; which applies is an interpretation. Claire should not interpret; Amanda owns it.

incoming_message.text: Can the board just change the fence rules without asking us? I heard they want to ban wood fences.

available_context.text: Declaration 7.2: The Board may adopt and amend reasonable rules and regulations.
Declaration 12.1: This Declaration may be amended by owners holding 67% of the votes.

must: tells Luis Amanda will pick it up and roughly what happens next
may quote what 7.2 and 12.1 say without deciding which governs
must_not: decides whether the board can do it
asks Luis to re-explain to Amanda

cases.title: Amanda gives meeting execution to Paige
cases.scenario: The board president asks Amanda to set up the budget meeting on October 14. Amanda keeps the budget substance; Paige owns notice, agenda, packet, and minutes. Notice requirements are in the bylaws; Amanda should not invent a notice period.

incoming_message.text: Let's do the 2027 budget meeting on October 14 at the clubhouse, 6pm. Can you set it up?

available_context.text: Draft 2027 budget prepared by Kat, v2 dated 9/22, not yet reviewed by the board.
Bylaws 4.3: Notice of board meetings must be given as required by law.

must: confirms the date back
says Paige will handle notice, agenda, and packet
says Amanda will get the draft budget ready for the packet
must_not: states a specific notice-day requirement not in the documents

cases.title: Paige returns board action items to Amanda
cases.scenario: After the September board meeting Paige has the draft minutes. Two action items belong to operations. Paige hands them to Amanda with exactly what the board directed, not a paraphrase that loses the limits.

incoming_message.text: Minutes for the 9/23 meeting are drafted. Route the action items.

available_context.text: Motion carried 4-0: obtain three bids for the north perimeter fence repair, not to exceed $18,000, and report at the October meeting.
Board directed management to ask the pool vendor for a written plan to fix the recurring chlorine alarm.
Board approved the 9/23 agenda and prior minutes.

must: both operational items with the board's limits (three bids, $18,000 cap, report in October)
notes the minutes are still a draft
must_not: routes the procedural item M3 as an action

cases.title: Phoebe requests fact confirmation before publishing
cases.scenario: Phoebe's October newsletter draft says pool resurfacing finishes October 1. The contractor's email says early October, not confirmed. Phoebe must ask the owner (Amanda) to confirm before print, and write the copy with the unknown kept unknown.

incoming_message.text: Finalize the pool item for the October newsletter.

available_context.text: BlueLine Pools email 9/19: resurfacing should finish in early October, weather permitting; no firm date.
Newsletter draft: 'Great news: the pool reopens October 1!'

must: asks Amanda to confirm the date with BlueLine before print
rewrites the item as early October, weather permitting, with a promise to share the date

cases.title: Amanda handles a routine issue without escalating to Ed
cases.scenario: A board member reports a broken sprinkler head at the front entrance. The landscaper is under contract and repairs are in scope. This is Amanda's to handle; Ed should not appear.

incoming_message.text: Sprinkler at the front entrance is shooting water into the street again. Can someone get GreenEdge out?

available_context.text: GreenEdge Landscaping contract: irrigation repairs included, response within 3 business days.

must: Amanda owns it: will send GreenEdge a work request
says repairs are in the contract
gives the contract response window without inventing a date
must_not: mentions Ed or asks for approval

cases.title: Amanda recognizes a financial posting that needs Ed's approval
cases.scenario: Kat forwards the treasurer's request to reclass a $4,200 pool pump invoice from operating to reserves and post it this month. Moving money between funds needs board authorization; the posting needs Ed's approval; Kat prepares.

incoming_message.text: Harold wants the $4,200 pool pump invoice reclassed from operating repairs to the reserve fund and posted this month. OK to go ahead?

available_context.text: Invoice BLP-5521, $4,200, pool pump replacement, coded to 5210 Pool Repairs (operating), paid 9/12.
No board motion on record authorizing reserve use for the pump.

must: do not post yet
reserve use needs a board motion (none on record)
Kat prepares the entry; Ed approves the posting
must_not: reports it as posted or reclassed
treats the treasurer's email alone as board authorization

cases.title: Board member asks Amanda about work Paige performed
cases.scenario: A board member asks Amanda whether the annual meeting notice went out. Paige did it and the shared record shows it. Amanda should answer from the record and credit Paige, not deflect.

incoming_message.text: Did the annual meeting notice go out? I know Paige was handling it.

shared_work_context.what: Annual meeting notice mailed first-class to 412 owners
Notice posted to the homeowner portal

must: yes, mailed 9/12 to 412 owners and posted to the portal
credits Paige
must_not: adds facts not in the record (return count, certified mail)

cases.title: Board member asks Paige about a payment Emma handled
cases.scenario: While Paige is assembling the packet, the treasurer asks whether GreenEdge's August invoice was paid. Emma paid it; the record shows it. Paige answers from the record and credits Emma.

incoming_message.text: Before the packet goes out, was GreenEdge's August invoice paid? They told Priscilla they hadn't been.

shared_work_context.what: GreenEdge invoice GE-0826, $3,150, paid by ACH

must: paid 9/5 by ACH, $3,150, GE-0826
credits Emma
offers to have Emma send GreenEdge the remittance detail
must_not: says it is Emma's area so she can't say
asks Harold to contact accounting himself

cases.title: Work that needs a human in person
cases.scenario: A homeowner wants someone to walk the drainage problem behind her house with her. The AI team cannot attend. This goes to the Community Manager role, not to a named person's desk, with the context so she is not re-asked.

incoming_message.text: The common-area drain behind 14 Heron Ct floods my yard every time it rains. Photos attached. Can someone come look at it with me?

available_context.text: Three photos attached showing standing water at the rear common-area drain.

must: acknowledges the photos specifically
says the community manager will reach out to set a time
must_not: promises a specific person or time
proposes a meeting Amanda would attend
asks her to resend the photos

cases.title: Fee waiver needs the board, not Ed
cases.scenario: A homeowner asks Amanda to waive a $150 late fee. The board decides waivers. Amanda can bring it with a recommendation. This is not an Ed item.

incoming_message.text: I was in the hospital in August and missed the due date. Can you waive the $150 late fee?

available_context.text: Account paid in full every quarter since 2019; August assessment paid 9/9; late fee $150 assessed 9/1.

must: the board decides waivers
Amanda will bring it to the board with his payment history
warm, specific acknowledgment of the hospital stay

cases.title: Legal threat goes to Ed with Darby, no argument on the merits
cases.scenario: A homeowner with an open fence violation writes that his attorney will contact Bedrock. Legal matters route to Ed; Darby coordinates counsel. Amanda acknowledges without arguing the violation.

incoming_message.text: This fence violation is harassment. My attorney will be contacting you.

available_context.text: Violation V-3310 (fence stain), courtesy notice 2 sent 9/10.

must: short, calm acknowledgment
says the message has been passed to the team that handles legal matters
must_not: states a legal position or §209 determination

cases.title: Balance discrepancy goes to Kat, not Ed
cases.scenario: The treasurer asks why the reserve balance on the bank statement differs from the financials. That is an accounting review for Kat. No posting is proposed yet, so Ed is not involved.

incoming_message.text: The reserve account statement shows $412,880 but the August financials say $405,130. Which is right?

must: Kat will reconcile the two and explain the difference
does not guess the cause as fact (timing is only a possibility)
must_not: asks Harold to resend the figures

cases.title: Vendor asks where to send an invoice
cases.scenario: A new vendor asks where invoices go. That is Emma's pipeline. No Ed.

incoming_message.text: Finished the pole light repair. Who do I send the invoice to?

must: tells him Emma in accounts payable handles invoices and how to send it

cases.title: Prospective community asks for pricing
cases.scenario: A board president from another community asks Amanda what Bedrock charges. Maggie owns prospect conversations; pricing needs Ed. Amanda should not quote a number.

incoming_message.text: We're unhappy with our current management company. What would Bedrock charge for 300 homes?

must: warm response; Maggie will reach out to learn about the community
no number quoted

cases.title: Mid-thread handoff to Annie keeps the context
cases.scenario: Claire has exchanged three messages with a homeowner about a fence application: height, material, and that the survey is attached. The homeowner now asks whether it will be approved. Claire hands to Annie with everything, so the homeowner is not re-asked.

governance_bodies.name: Architectural Control Committee
governance_bodies.scope: approve or deny exterior modifications under the ACC Guidelines
governance_bodies.source: Declaration Art. 8 and ACC Guidelines (demo community)

conversation_history.text: I want to put in a 6 ft cedar privacy fence along the back.
Thanks! Do you have a survey showing where it will go?
Yes, attached the survey with the fence line marked.

incoming_message.text: So will it get approved? We want to start in two weeks.

available_context.text: ACC Guidelines 4.1: Rear fences up to 6 ft; wood or approved composite; stained a neutral color.

must: Annie handles ACC and has the survey and details
the committee decides; no approval implied
may note what 4.1 says
must_not: asks Sam to resend the survey or restate the fence details

cases.title: A human is already the assigned owner: name her, do not re-route
cases.scenario: A homeowner follows up on the drainage walk-through. The work item is already assigned to the Community Manager (Martha Bravo), who scheduled the visit. Naming Martha is correct here because she is the assigned owner; re-routing to a generic queue would lose the thread.

conversation_history.text: The common-area drain behind 14 Heron Ct floods my yard. Can someone come look?
Thanks for the photos. Our community manager will reach out to set a time to walk it with you.

incoming_message.text: Is someone still coming out to look at the drain? I have not heard anything since.

shared_work_context.what: Drainage walk-through at 14 Heron Ct scheduled with Grace Kim for Tuesday 9/30 at 10am

must: yes: Martha Bravo, the community manager, is scheduled for Tuesday 9/30 at 10am
apologizes briefly that the confirmation did not reach her
must_not: re-routes to a generic queue as if nothing were scheduled
